name: James
label: Factory Records
lede: James turned down a Factory album, toured with the Smiths, lived on T-shirt money for years, and had to wait 42 years for a No. 1 studio album.

eras.title: A dancer from the student union
eras.text: James came out of Whalley Range, Manchester, and out of long improvised jams that nobody planned. Within a year of forming they'd played the Haçienda with New Order and had Tony Wilson asking for an album. They settled on the name James in August 1982, after a short spell as Tribal Outlook.

years.h: Paul Gilbertson talks Jim Glennie into buying a bass
years.p: [[Paul Gilbertson|25f05a37-2fdd-4ce4-9caa-db79510f1091]] got Glennie, by his own description a football hooligan, to learn bass. With [[Gavan Whelan|07cdd05b-531a-4006-97e0-534fb267036b]] on drums they played as Venereal and the Diseases, Volume Distortion and Model Team International.

years.h: Gilbertson spots Tim Booth dancing and hires him to dance
years.p: [[Tim Booth|29714393-bafa-4ca5-a450-ab75f0070bc2]], a drama student at Manchester University, joined as the band's dancer before he became its singer.
years.xp:
In Glennie's telling, he and Gilbertson were stealing Booth's beer when they met him. Within a week they were supporting [[Orange Juice|e598d30e-4ce1-402e-94a7-6f44779da6b7]] in Sheffield, Booth on tambourine.

Early on, promoters billed them as "James (Not a poet)" after Booth read his lyrics at a show.

years.h: Mike Pickering puts them on the Haçienda bill with New Order
years.p: On [[Mike Pickering|5da7585b-4ac0-420f-8c58-9bb8522b459c]]'s recommendation, James played with New Order, [[The Durutti Column|aaddb5e3-f8a5-4a9d-8674-f885112ecf0e]] and [[Section 25|82e26f64-813d-4b22-a442-44d182f7f9eb]]. Tony Wilson saw the film of the show and offered an album deal.
years.xp: The band said no to an album and asked for a three-track EP instead.

years.h: They give Factory the songs they like least
years.p: Jimone is three songs in six and a half minutes, recorded with Chris Nagle at Strawberry Studios, Stockport, in August.
years.xp:
According to Stuart Maconie's band biography Folklore, James deliberately recorded what they thought were their weakest songs, afraid the studio would ruin their best ones.

'Fire So Close' came back reworked as 'Why So Close' on Stutter.

eras.title: On tour with the Smiths
eras.text: Both Johnny Marr and Morrissey owned the first EP, and The Smiths took James on the road. Behind the press attention, the band lost a founder to drugs, and Booth and Glennie joined a sect called Lifewave whose rules strained the band.

years.src: Head Heritage · Vice · Wikipedia: James II
years.h: Their guitar teacher, Larry Gott, replaces Gilbertson
years.p: Gilbertson, who started the band, left; Head Heritage says he "became a victim of drugs." [[Larry Gott|f2bc83a2-e8ec-40af-a93b-34f9f38af507]] had been the band's guitar tutor.
years.xp:
Gott on his first rehearsals: "I didn't know what key it was in. I didn't know anything."

He soon worked out the band's method: hours of wordless jamming, taped and picked over later. In his estimate the music came together 10 to 20 percent of the time.

years.h: 'Hymn from a Village' puts James on the NME cover
years.p: James II, two songs recorded at Strawberry in October 1984, reached No. 2 on the indie chart and stayed 18 weeks.

years.h: The Smiths take James on the Meat Is Murder tour
years.p: The tour ran from February into April. The Smiths covered James's 'What's the World' live, and their version came out on a live format of 'Last Night I Dreamt That Somebody Loved Me'.
years.xp:
When Morrissey had a headache, Glennie gave him a neck massage. "Back in those days we were a bunch of hippies," Glennie told Vice, so a massage was nothing unusual.

Morrissey's verdict, as Glennie remembers it: "Much better, thanks very much." Glennie adds that he was probably lying.

years.cap: James on the front cover of NME, 1985
years.src: Wikipedia: Stutter · Wikipedia: James · Head Heritage
years.h: James turns down a Factory album and signs to Sire
years.p: Worried that Factory cared more about image than anything else, the band went to [[Seymour Stein|3a95e565-673e-430b-abb4-e17229320fdf]]'s Sire, via Blanco y Negro. Factory put both EPs together as Village Fire.

eras.title: Thirty quid a week
eras.text: Sire wanted hits and James didn't deliver them. What kept the band alive was the live show and the merch stand: the flower T-shirts sold better than the records.

years.h: Patti Smith's guitarist Lenny Kaye produces Stutter
years.p: [[Lenny Kaye|47455aa4-c71e-4662-a775-33b81fcf0a37]] recorded it at Amazon Studios in Liverpool, January to March 1986, with Gil Norton engineering. It reached No. 68, which frustrated Sire and Stein.
years.xp:
Reviews split. Dave Haslam in NME heard a "cleanly delivered debut LP, gleaming with creativity and confidence." Chris Roberts in Sounds called it "an interesting but club-footed student exercise."

It still made year-end lists in The Face, NME and Spex.

years.h: The flower T-shirts keep James afloat
years.p: Through the late 1980s the band earned more from merchandise than from records. Booth says that for about five years they made around 30 quid a week each, about the same as the dole.
years.xp:
Thatcher's Enterprise Allowance scheme let them go professional and tour without losing benefits. Gott regularly siphoned petrol from cars around the neighbourhood to get them to gigs.

Glennie remembers getting to Oxford in the back of a butcher's van, illegally, freezing, with the drums set up and blood everywhere.

years.h: Strip-mine reaches No. 90, and James finds the exit clause
years.p: The band reached for more conventional songs to please Sire. Low on money and promotion, they found a clause that let them out of the contract.

years.h: Gavan Whelan fights Tim Booth on stage and leaves
years.p: The original drummer was gone after an onstage fight with Booth. David Baynton-Power took over months later.
years.xp: Whelan liked Rush and Deep Purple, which put him at odds with Glennie and Gilbertson from the start. Afterwards he worked as a drum roadie for [[Primal Scream|55704c38-224f-4b75-b29f-d43653f8bc9a]] and [[Happy Mondays|01f4fb92-6bf0-4de5-83dc-3fe194e763bf]].

eras.title: Everybody sits down
eras.text: With a bank loan, a live album and a seven-piece line-up, James went back to the indie labels and found the song that carried them into the charts. It took two tries.

years.h: A bank loan pays for a live album taped in Bath
years.p: An RBS loan and [[Rough Trade|4f4b0013-1704-4936-a769-e6e8a6e08ff8]] backed One Man Clapping, recorded at the Moles club in Bath. It went to No. 1 on the indie chart.

years.h: Saul Davies is recruited from an amateur blues night
years.p: Davies on guitar, violin and percussion, [[Mark Hunter|ebcf0fd3-dc24-4808-a34b-ad888919ff60]] on keyboards and Andy Diagram on trumpet, ex-[[The Pale Fountains|f5c83ec1-7d76-42ff-b727-3c85878b9766]], made James a seven-piece.

years.big: "We'd just written a Eurovision song contest song"
years.h: The first 'Sit Down' runs 8:39 and stops at No. 77
years.p: Glennie on the night they wrote it, three chords round and round. The Rough Trade single made No. 8 in John Peel's Festive Fifty, and Haçienda crowds sat down on the floor.
years.xp: Booth has said the song is about feeling alone in his twenties and reading Doris Lessing. The Musicians' Union banned the original video, Uncut reports, over a detail involving the drum stool.

years.h: Gold Mother lands in the middle of Madchester
years.p: 'How Was It for You', a remixed 'Come Home' and 'Lose Control' all went top 40. Two sold-out G-Mex shows in Manchester followed.
years.xp: Before it came out, Rough Trade's [[Geoff Travis|70437714-3183-4916-947f-e5ba2154d16a]] told them James could reach 20,000 to 30,000 people. The band bought back the album rights and took it to Fontana.

years.src: Wikipedia: Sit Down · Uncut · Wikipedia: James
years.h: Re-recorded, 'Sit Down' gets stuck at No. 2 behind Chesney Hawkes
years.p: Gil Norton and Steve Power produced the new, shorter version. It was the 20th best-selling single of 1991 and sold 600,000 in the UK.
years.xp:
"It took three days to give the song some bollocks," Booth told Uncut of the Norton sessions. Gold Mother was reissued with it and went on to sell ten times what Travis had predicted.

In 2013 it came fourth in a BBC Radio 2 poll of the greatest songs that never reached No. 1. [[Coldplay|cc197bad-dc9c-440d-a5b5-d52ba2e14234]] played it at One Love Manchester in 2017.

eras.title: Thirty thousand at Alton Towers, then Eno
eras.text: James got as big as they had ever been, then toured acoustic as Neil Young's support in the US and went into the studio with Brian Eno, the producer they'd first asked for back in 1986.

years.h: Seven goes to No. 2 and James goes to America
years.p: 'Sound' made the top 10. The band followed it with its first US tour.

years.h: Thirty thousand people at a theme park, live on Radio 1
years.p: James sold out a show for 30,000 at Alton Towers, broadcast live by BBC Radio 1. Andy Diagram left afterwards.

years.src: Wikipedia: Laid · Big Issue · Wikipedia: James
years.h: Brian Eno, seven years after they first asked
years.p: Laid was recorded in Wrexham and at Real World early in 1993. It reached No. 3 in the UK, and college radio pushed the title song to No. 61 on the Hot 100.
years.xp:
"This guy knows what he's doing. I don't need to make people do 12 takes any more," Booth told the Big Issue. Laid went gold in the UK and the US and shipped more than 600,000 copies.

AllMusic later called its stripped-down sound arguably the band's artistic peak. NME was cooler, saying the production made "un-songs."

years.h: The jams Eno kept become Wah Wah
years.p: Improvisations from the Laid sessions, mixed by Eno with Booth's vocals added later. It reached No. 11.

eras.title: Tax bills, Lollapalooza and a goodbye
eras.text: Gott left, the manager left, the taxman arrived and Booth made a record with Angelo Badalamenti. James came back with two top-two albums anyway, then lost their singer.

years.h: Larry Gott steps away to be with his family
years.p: Manager Martine McDonagh left too, a £250,000 tax bill arrived, and recording moved to Baynton-Power's house. [[Adrian Oxaal|9813f505-abdc-41a1-a604-78c1301226d0]], ex-Sharkboy, took over on guitar.

years.h: Whiplash goes top 10 and gold
years.p: 'She's a Star' made the top 10 too. Michael Kulas joined on rhythm guitar for the tour.

years.h: Booth hurts his neck dancing; James joins Lollapalooza instead
years.p: The injury on a US stage cancelled dates, and the band went out on Lollapalooza.

years.h: Millionaires enters at No. 2
years.p: It went gold and sold more than 150,000 copies, below what had been predicted.

years.big: "A lot of addiction, a lot of unconscious hostility"
years.h: Tim Booth leaves to work on his own projects
years.p: Booth's later explanation to the Big Issue for walking out, after Pleased to Meet You stopped at No. 11, the band's lowest placing on Fontana.

years.h: The farewell tour ends at the Manchester Evening News Arena
years.p: Gott and Diagram came back for it, and Eno joined them on stage at Wembley. The last night became Getting Away with It... Live.

eras.title: Zsasz, then the phone call
eras.text: Booth made solo records and turned up in a Batman film. In November 2006 he got together with Glennie and Gott to jam, and the songs that came out of it brought the band back.

years.cap: Tim Booth on stage at Guilfest, Guildford
years.h: Booth plays Victor Zsasz in Batman Begins
years.p: A year after his solo album Bone, made with Lee Muddy Baker. He voiced the character in the video game too.

years.cap: The reunited James in a 2008 press photo
years.h: The Laid line-up reunites and the dates sell out at once
years.p: Booth's website announced it in January. Five dates became seven; Andy Diagram was back on trumpet by the summer festivals.

years.h: Hey Ma, the first album in seven years, reaches No. 10
years.p: The spring tour that followed was released as Live in 2008, sold only at the merch stand and limited to 5,000.

years.cap: James on stage at Positivus festival, Latvia
years.h: An album in two halves: The Night Before and The Morning After
years.p: The second mini-album followed on August 2. In North America they came out together.

eras.title: Forty years, then a No. 1
eras.text: The reunited James has now outlasted its first run. They found an unlikely audience in Greece and, in 2024, topped the UK chart with a studio album for the first time.

years.h: La Petite Mort, partly written in Greece
years.p: James had become hugely popular in Greece after one 2001 Athens gig, Vice reported. In October they played the Super League Grand Final at Old Trafford.

years.h: Larry Gott takes a break and Adrian Oxaal returns
years.p: Oceansize's Mike Vennart covered one show. Oxaal has been in the band since.

years.h: After 42 years, Yummy is James's first No. 1 studio album
years.p: Their 18th album went straight to the top of the UK chart. A June tour followed with [[Razorlight|f2cb0435-d643-4fab-9587-fdb0279330a7]] in support.

years.h: The first US headline tour in 15 years plays Laid in full
years.p: Eighteen dates in September and October, nine musicians, two sets with a break. A live album, Live at the Acropolis, was announced too.
